PASS applies only to the revised, explicitly limited A–E theorem with the specified standard Fubini–Study form. The complete limited argument is established under the task’s granted maximal-subsolution characterization and attainment. original_S12_completed=false; original_inverse_realization_unresolved=true. The supplied original INCONCLUSIVE report, old targets, complete notes, n7 counterexample, and historical candidate=false remain unchanged. Their verdicts, receipts, hashes and program outputs were not used as mathematical premises.

A. Canonical subtraction covers every one-sided competitor. For u≤ell_E+K, w=u−ell_E is defined first outside S=Supp(E), satisfies h_E+dd^c w≥0 and is bounded above. The epsilon-logarithm and truncation construction extends w+rho as a genuine psh function. It also retains the precise nonclosed inequality: R_epsilon=dd^c v_epsilon is an order-zero positive current; outside S, R_epsilon+h_E−dd^c rho is positive, and on S the smooth correction has zero coefficient-measure mass. Restricting these coefficient measures to S and its complement therefore proves positivity globally. Local L1 convergence preserves that exact bound. Canonical uniqueness patches the extensions and proves u=ell_E+w everywhere, including poles. Conversely, every genuine residual potential has finite supremum and yields a genuine one-sided potential. Ordinary equivalence corresponds exactly to bounded residuals. Actual domination h+dd^c u≥[E] also gives this representation by distributional subtraction. E=0 reduces to the identity correspondence.

The extended-measure identity is valid even when mass is infinite. On relatively compact charts outside S, use common strict-superlevel restrictions where both potentials are bounded. The bounded nonclosed product expansions, smooth-shift invariance and plurifine locality identify the restricted products. Exhausting these loci identifies the positive top-degree Borel measures without subtracting infinite quantities. Both measures give S zero mass. Consequently every subsolution inequality transports in both directions. The task grant applies to the positive metric h_E and proves B_leq=b_(h_E)(f), with an actual attaining potential. General L1 data receive no additional ordinary-type, stretching, finite-mass or exact-equation conclusion.

B. For every envelope competitor v≤0, its residual w satisfies integral w^+ dV≤integral(−ell_E)dV. Fixed coordinate balls, bounded quadratic corrections and submean inequalities give a uniform bound on sup w. Thus ell_E≤phi_E≤ell_E+K. The upper bound survives usc regularization and preserves −infinity at every divisor pole. Convolution and convex regularized maxima retain the exact background inequality with errors tending to zero; countable selection and monotone local convergence produce the genuine envelope. For u~ell_E~phi_E, the witnesses a_t=phi_E−tK_u prove the original stretching inequality for every real t≥1. The reverse containment follows directly from the defining order restriction. No envelope-equality characterization replaces stretching.

The alternative arguments in n1–n3 also check out. The normalized L1 contradiction uses local compactness to obtain a global psh limit equal to −1, then fixed-radius submean estimates contradict supremum zero. The bound on a nonempty set away from S gives the uniform envelope bound. The alternative witnesses ell_E−tA−(t−1)B satisfy the same all-t definition canonically.

C. The analytic applications have the required hypotheses. [Kołodziej–Nguyen, Theorem 0.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.5491v2) supplies continuous existence, and [Nguyen, Corollary 0.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.00891v1) supplies uniqueness of the positive scalar. Neither application requires potential uniqueness for the equation without an exponential term. Nonzero bounded densities, after multiplying by dV/alpha^n, belong to Lp(alpha^n), p>1. Their operators are twice the task operator, so multiplying source potentials by two preserves the background and equation. For smooth strictly positive f, [Tosatti–Weinkove, Corollary 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.1390v2) applies separately to h and h_E with F=log(f dV/alpha^n); source potentials are multiplied by 2π. Bounded truncation is eventually stationary, so b_alpha(f)=c_alpha(f). A smooth residual solution yields ell_E+w, its actual finite extended equation, and mass c_(h_E)(f) integral f dV. A and B then prove equality and attainment in all three specified classes.

The strict scalar comparison is valid without nefness or semipositivity of beta_E. If the scalars were equal, a=ell_E+w−v would satisfy dd^c a wedge Q=0 outside S, where Q=sum eta^j wedge sigma^(n−1−j) has a strictly positive principal matrix. Closure of Q is unnecessary. The supplied exponential barrier has Lb>0 on its annulus for sufficiently large A. The weak minimum argument and the derivative contradiction at the touching zero prove the strong maximum conclusion. Since a tends uniformly to −infinity near S, its maximum is attained inside a complementary component. Constancy there contradicts approach to its nonempty boundary in S.

The independent n4 proof is also valid. [Gauduchon’s Theorem 2](https://numdam.org/item/AST_1985__126__129_0.pdf) and its adjoint-kernel proof apply in complex dimension n≥2, despite the surface-specific title. They give the smooth positive calibrated test T=σ B^(n−1)/Z. Arithmetic–geometric mean yields integral A wedge T≥(c_(h_E)/c_h)^(1/n), while integration by parts gives integral A wedge T=1−I. Here I=integral beta_E wedge T=integral_[E] T satisfies 0<I<1. This is an actual divisor pairing with a smooth test, and proves the stated strict gap.

D. For an initially dominated nonzero divisor E_0, choose 0<δ≤1 small enough that h−δ beta_(E_0)>0. Actual domination remains valid for δE_0. The L1 distribution u−δ ell_(E_0) has the exact residual lower Hessian bound and a genuine canonical representative; its finite supremum places u in the corresponding entire one-sided class. A and strictness give b_h(f)≤c_(h−δ beta_(E_0))(f)<b_h(f), a contradiction. This argument permits excess or infinite extended mass and imposes no residual positivity on the original divisor.

E. With the newly specified FS form, local Poincaré–Lelong gives dd^c ell=[D]−kappa with precisely the task normalization. Only horizontal degree m and vertical degree k survive in the binomial expansion. Hence H^N=CV0 R dV and H_E^N=CV0(1−lambda)^k R dV. Zero potentials solve the smooth equations; scalar uniqueness and the task characterization establish global maximality, including against arbitrary genuine singular subsolutions. The potential lambda ell attains every restricted maximum, has the actual component lambda[D], and solves the claimed finite extended equation. B gives its genuine stretching membership. An arbitrary smooth probability dV is fully accounted for by R=mu/dV.

Under the explicit antecedent v_-(h0)=0, bounded factor pullbacks have product masses C M_j and C(1−lambda)^k M_j with M_j tending to zero. Positivity proves both product infima equal zero. If h0 were closed, bounded Bedford–Taylor recursion gives (h0+dd^c w)^m−h0^m=dd^c(w sum_r (h0+dd^c w)^r wedge h0^(m−1−r)); Stokes fixes every bounded mass at V0>0. Therefore h0, H and H_E are nonclosed under that antecedent. No factor satisfying it is constructed or imported. The original connectedness convention is respected; the optional finite-component extension in n6 follows componentwise from the same common scalar. The low-dimensional conditional cases noted there are vacuous.

The preserved n7 counterexample genuinely rejects the old normalization-only E. For kappa=kappa_FS+dd^c psi, sufficiently small positive epsilon makes both kappa and eta=kappa−lambda kappa_FS positive, while closed Stokes keeps integral kappa^k=1. Choose the chart origin away from D so that dd^c psi=epsilon kappa_FS there. The advertised potential lambda ell then has density ratio eta^k/kappa^k=((1+epsilon−lambda)/(1+epsilon))^k>(1−lambda)^k. Its total mass nevertheless equals the claimed restricted mass, so it cannot dominate that threshold density. The bounded residual −lambda psi produces the corrected attainer lambda ell−lambda psi. The diagnostic 36/121−1/4=23/484 is correct; global positivity relies on sufficiently small epsilon, not the diagnostic’s particular value. The revised FS hypothesis excludes this perturbation and constitutes the declared input correction.

The current literature qualification is accurate. [Alehyane–Lu–Salouf, Definition 2.13 and Theorem 5.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.02339v1) require a semipositive big background and a model reference satisfying P_theta[phi]=phi and P_(epsilon theta)(phi) not identically −infinity. Here theta=h is positive; ordinary equivalence identifies the model envelopes, and epsilon h−beta_E>0 for epsilon sufficiently close to one makes ell_E an admissible competitor below phi_E. Smooth positive data meet the nonzero Lp hypothesis. Thus their theorem already covers the ordinary-existence portion. The additional lower-volume hypothesis introduced for Theorem 5.8 is not a hypothesis of 5.7. This literature note is supporting context, not an indispensable premise of A–E or recursive certification of that paper’s foundations.

The historical overlap claims also have the stated limits. [Darvas–Di Nezza–Lu, Theorem 1.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1705.05796v3) covers the closed Kähler case with a positive-mass model reference, small unbounded locus and an appropriately mass-normalized Lp density. [BEGZ, Theorem 3.1 and Section 3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2) supplies closed big-class existence with measure mass equal to the class volume and explicitly deletes effective divisors from the non-pluripolar equation. These results do not establish the nonclosed general-L1 conclusions or identify their full-mass classes with the task’s stretching class. No priority or blanket literature-open claim is certified.

All external premises below were checked against freshly opened primary texts. BGL Section 2.1 and GL2’s bounded construction support the finite-level applications. BGL Section 2.2 requires bounded mass property and is not applied. BEGZ’s global Kähler finiteness theorem is likewise not applied. Harmless wording clarifications: the removal neighborhoods are taken locally on relatively compact coordinate sets; at t=1 the stretching expression means a_1≤u, with the zero-weight term omitted. No substantive repair of the revised A–E proof is needed. Original S12 still lacks either an actual global-threshold divisor realization or a substantive converse counterexample satisfying its antecedents.
